title: Review: A simple model of the atom, symbols, relative atomic mass, electronic charge and isotopes
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.1.1-c36, 4.1.1-c32, 4.1.1-c06, 4.1.1-c16. Clues: 4.1.1-c36 written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.1.1-c32 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.1-c06 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.1-c16 first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.1.1-q09, 4.1.1-q14, 4.1.1-q25, 4.1.1-q05, 4.1.1-q49, 4.1.1-q21, 4.1.1-q08, 4.1.1-q12, 4.1.1-q19, 4.1.1-q02, 4.1.1-q48, 4.1.1-q24. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Electronic structure
items.clue: The arrangement written as numbers such as 2,8,1 for sodium.

items.label: Isotopes
items.clue: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.

items.label: Chemical reaction
items.clue: A change that always forms one or more new substances and often involves a detectable energy change.

items.label: Chromatography
items.clue: A physical process that separates substances in a mixture by how they move with a solvent through paper.

questions.stem: Magnesium burns in oxygen to form magnesium oxide. Which symbol equation represents this reaction correctly?

options.text: Mg + O₂ → MgO
Mg + O₂ → MgO₂
2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
2Mg + 2O₂ → 2MgO

questions.explanation: Two Mg atoms and two O atoms on each side, with the products on the right.

questions.stem: Copper sulfate solution is left in an evaporating basin until crystals form. What has happened?

options.text: The copper sulfate evaporated, leaving the water behind
The water has evaporated, leaving the copper sulfate
The copper sulfate has reacted to make a blue solid
The water was condensed on a lid and collected

questions.explanation: In crystallisation the solvent evaporates and the solute is left as crystals.

questions.stem: What did the experimental work of James Chadwick provide evidence for?

options.text: Protons inside the nucleus, about 20 years after this was accepted
Neutrons inside the nucleus, about 20 years after it was accepted
Electrons, which had been found long before the nuclear model
The nucleus itself, at the centre of every atom

questions.explanation: Chadwick's work showed that neutrons exist within the nucleus.

questions.stem: What must happen in every chemical reaction?

options.text: A detectable energy change must be measured
One or more new substances must always be formed
A gas or a change of colour must be seen
Two elements must join to make a compound

questions.explanation: Chemical reactions always involve the formation of one or more new substances.

questions.stem: A mixture of ethanol and water is separated by fractional distillation. Why does this method work?

options.text: The two liquids boil at different temperatures
One is a solid dissolved in the other liquid
Heating the mixture makes new substances form
Water evaporates away, leaving the ethanol

questions.explanation: Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids using their different boiling points.

questions.stem: In the scattering experiment a few alpha particles were deflected straight back. Why did this change the atomic model?

options.text: It showed that the whole atom is filled with positive charge
It showed that electrons are far heavier than was thought
The plum pudding model could not explain such large deflections
It proved that atoms are tiny spheres that cannot be split

questions.explanation: A spread-out positive charge could not turn a fast alpha particle around.

questions.stem: A compound has the formula MgO. What is its name?

options.text: Magnesium oxygen
Magnesium oxide
Magnesium dioxide
Magnesium monoxide

questions.explanation: The metal keeps its name and oxygen becomes oxide.

questions.stem: A mixture of ethanol and water is separated by fractional distillation. Which statement is correct?

options.text: New substances are made because the mixture has been heated up
The ethanol collected has different properties from before
The two liquids react with each other as they are heated
No new substances are made, as no chemical reaction happens

questions.explanation: Separation methods are physical processes, so no new substances are made.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the plum pudding model of the atom?

options.text: A ball of negative charge with positive particles inside it
A ball of positive charge with negative electrons embedded in it
A small positive nucleus with electrons around the outside
A solid sphere of matter that cannot be divided at all

questions.explanation: This is the specification's description of the plum pudding model.

questions.stem: Which option gives the chemical symbols correctly?

options.text: So is sodium and Ox is oxygen
Na is sodium and O is oxygen
N is sodium and O is oxygen
Na is sodium, O2 is oxygen

questions.explanation: Na represents an atom of sodium and O an atom of oxygen.

questions.stem: Ink is spotted on chromatography paper and a solvent runs up it. Why do the dyes separate?

options.text: They move different distances with the solvent
The darkest dye always travels the furthest
The paper traps each dye as a filter would
The paper reacts with the dyes to make new ones

questions.explanation: Each dye is held by the paper and carried by the solvent to a different extent.

questions.stem: What did later experiments show about the positive charge of a nucleus?

options.text: It can be divided into whole numbers of identical charges
It is carried by one single particle found by James Chadwick
It comes from the neutrons, which each carry a small charge
It is spread evenly through the atom, not in a nucleus

questions.explanation: Each of these identical smaller charges was named a proton.
